And there is an obvious problem with the statement "The wage gap is a big fat lie"... First it's a "big fat lie," then it's a "meaningless statistic." He doesn't make any effort to separate the narrative from the statistic, which measures exactly what it intends to. Not only is the statistic accurate, but the gap can be decreased without giving every woman a raise. Norway for example has a much better parental leave & childcare system than the US, and their pay gap is smaller--partly due to women being able to better maintain their jobs when starting a family.

The author dismisses these benefits as "unfair advantages" that feminists are trying to get men to pay for using faulty statistics. Yet they don't do anything for the faulty "same pay for same work" narrative. Instead they present solutions to the actual reasons which even the author says causes the wage gap. He should have stuck to his guns and focused on the truly faulty narratives adopted by feminists, rather than try to undermine the body of issues entirely.
